description: Read, update, focus, and render text and node selections in Plate.

files.content:
--- title: Selection description: Read, update, focus, and render text and node selections in Plate. --- Plate stores selection in the editor model and projects text selection to the browser through the mounted editor. Use this guide for normal Plate reads, updates, focus, and rendering; use [Selection And DOM](/docs/plite/concepts/16-selection-and-dom) for low-level DOM coverage and browser repair behavior. ## Ownership The editor model is the single selection state. Each rendering layer derives its presentation from that state. | Job | Owner | | --- | --- | | Selection state, mapping, validation, reads, and updates | Plite core, reexported by `platejs` | | Native DOM selection, focus synchronization, and inactive paint | Plite React, inherited by `PlateContent` | | Exact node-selection highlighting and pointer-drag input | `NodeSelectionHighlight` and `NodeSelectionDrag` from `platejs/react` | | Focus markers, colors, borders, and stacking | Copied registry UI | ## Quick Start `editor.read.selection()` returns the active representative `Range` or `null`. For an exact node selection, use `selection.nodes()` or `selection.ranges()` instead of treating that representative range as exact membership. ```tsx title="selection.ts" showLineNumbers const range = editor.read.selection(); const expanded = editor.read.selection.isExpanded(); const selectedNodes = editor.read.selection.nodes(); const exactRanges = editor.read.selection.ranges(); editor.update.selection.set({ anchor: { path: [0, 0], offset: 0 }, focus: { path: [0, 0], offset: 5 }, }); editor.update.selection.setNodes([[0], [2]]); editor.update.selection.collapse({ edge: 'end' }); editor.update.selection.set(null); ``` | Model state | `selection()` | Exact membership | Browser presentation | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Text selection | One `Range` | `ranges()` returns that range | Native browser selection while the mounted editor is focused | | Node selection | One representative `Range` | `nodes()` and `ranges()` return every selected node | Plate node-selection primitives; the native selection stays empty | | No selection | `null` | Empty arrays | None | Use [Editor Methods](/docs/editor-methods) for editor access inside React and [Selection API](/docs/plite/api/locations/selection) for the complete query and validation contracts. ## Focus and Native Selection Updating the model selection does not require direct DOM selection writes. When an action should return input to the editor, set the selection and focus the mounted editor explicitly: ```tsx editor.update.selection.set(range); editor.api.dom.focus(); ``` Mouse, keyboard, touch, composition, and native input can move the browser selection. The mounted editor imports those changes into the model and exports model updates back to the DOM. Application code should not patch `window.getSelection()` for normal editor behavior. ## Inactive Selection Plite `Editable` renders an inactive selection when focus moves to a marked control. The behavior is built in; it does not require a prop, plugin, kit, or copied selection state. ### Mark a Focus Target Add `data-plite-keep-selection-visible` to a focusable control or any composed ancestor: ```tsx
``` The exact `Editable` that loses focus reads its live canonical selection. An expanded range renders a highlight. A collapsed range renders a caret. Focus returning to the editor or moving to an unmarked target removes the inactive paint. ### Style the Paint Plite publishes neutral output hooks. Product CSS owns their appearance: ```css [data-plite-inactive-selection] { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 25%, transparent); } [data-plite-inactive-selection-caret] { width: 2px; background: var(--primary); } ``` The copied `Editor` registry component already styles both hooks. ### Focus Behavior | Focus target | Inactive paint | | --- | --- | | Marked control or composed ancestor | One highlight or caret from the originating `Editable` | | The editor | None; the browser owns the active selection | | Any unmarked control | None | | Window blur or missing focus target | None | The marker controls presentation only. It does not modify the document, selection, history, clipboard, or collaboration state. ## Node Selection Rendering Exact node selection is model state, not a native browser range. The copied `Editor` composes `NodeSelectionHighlight` and `NodeSelectionDrag` after `PlateContent` to render selected blocks and support blank-space pointer drag. Use the [Node Selection components](/docs/api/core/plate-components#node-selection) for the DOM contract and the [Node Selection demo](/docs/examples/node-selection) for the copied Editor composition. Feature UI such as Block Menu reads the same exact node membership instead of maintaining another selected-node store. ## Related Selection Features Keep feature-specific behavior with the feature that owns it: | Need | Guide | | --- | --- | | Configure mark and inline boundary affinity | [Editing Behavior](/docs/editing-behavior#selection-behavior) and [Plugin Rules](/docs/plugin-rules#rulesselection) | | Apply context-menu actions to selected blocks | [Block Menu](/docs/block-menu) | | Search text with transient match highlights | [Find](/docs/find) | | Preserve selection while editing a link | [Link](/docs/link) | | Publish and render remote selections | [Collaboration](/docs/yjs) | | Build a tag-oriented select editor | [Multi Select](/docs/multi-select) | ## API Reference - [Selection API](/docs/plite/api/locations/selection) - [Selection methods](/docs/plite/api/transforms#selection-methods) - [Selection And DOM](/docs/plite/concepts/16-selection-and-dom) - [Node Selection components](/docs/api/core/plate-components#node-selection) Done. Plate code writes model selection; the mounted editor owns browser projection and presentation.
